formulaCard.title: Formulas (Markup on Selling Price)

explanation: Because selling price = cost + markup, and markup = % on SP × SP, we have: $$S = C + (r \times S)$$ where $r$ is the percent markup on SP as a decimal.
Solve for S: $S - rS = C \Rightarrow S(1 - r) = C$ ⇒ $$S = \frac{C}{1 - r}$$.
Thus, to find selling price when cost and % on SP are known, divide cost by (1 − r).
To find cost from selling price and % on SP: $C = S \times (1 - r)$.
These formulas are inverses of the cost‑based ones.

discoveryHook.scenario: Gap knows the jacket costs \$18 and they want a 21.74% markup on selling price. To find the price: since markup is 21.74% of SP, cost must be 78.26% of SP. So SP = \$18 ÷ 0.7826 ≈ \$23. The selling price is determined by dividing cost by the complement of the markup rate.

formulaCard.title: Cost from Selling Price (SP Base)

explanation: If selling price and percent markup on SP are known, cost is the complement part: $$C = S \times (1 - r)$$.
Because $S$ is 100%, cost = $(1 - r)$ of $S$.
This formula is straightforward: multiply SP by the percentage that cost represents.
No division needed; just multiply.
Always ensure $r$ is in decimal form.

visuals.title: Conversion Examples
visuals.caption: Conversions help when comparing profit margins reported in different ways.

explanation: To convert markup on cost ($r_c$) to markup on SP ($r_s$): $$r_s = \frac{r_c}{1 + r_c}$$.
To convert markup on SP ($r_s$) to markup on cost ($r_c$): $$r_c = \frac{r_s}{1 - r_s}$$.
These formulas follow from the relationships $S = C(1+r_c)$ and $C = S(1-r_s)$.
Use the blueprint aid (Understand → Solve → Conclude) for SP‑based markup problems, just as with cost‑based ones.
Carefully identify whether the given rate is on cost or on selling price before applying formulas.

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{\% on SP} = \frac{\text{\% on Cost}}{1 + \text{\% on Cost}}$$ $$\text{\% on Cost} = \frac{\text{\% on SP}}{1 - \text{\% on SP}}$$

examples.title: B – Why the formula works
examples.prompt: Explain why dividing by (1 + r_c) converts cost‑based to SP‑based markup.
steps: S = C(1 + r_c), and markup = r_c × C.
Percent on SP = (r_c × C) / (C(1 + r_c)) = r_c/(1 + r_c).
So you divide by (1 + r_c) because the selling price already contains that markup.
